topic: longitudinal and cross-thread workplace briefing systems that track new, open, resolved, and superseded work-item state over repeated cycles, with adaptive user-specific prioritization, reminder value, uncertainty presentation, and omission/repetition evaluation

gaps.description: This corpus does not directly evaluate a longitudinal workplace briefing that, across successive report cycles, distinguishes newly changed information from unchanged-but-still-open work while suppressing resolved or superseded information.
gaps.suggested_search_query: "incremental summarization" longitudinal workplace email briefing "open" resolved superseded state
gaps.resolution_notes: Still open. Incremental-processing evidence from news and clinical domains and stale-state evidence from workplace reminders do not directly evaluate repeated workplace briefings with explicit new, unchanged-open, resolved, and superseded work-item states.

gaps.description: This corpus does not establish how explicit user rules or response obligations interact with softer personalized importance, triage, reminder-value, or forgetting signals in briefing selection, nor whether separating these signal classes improves outcomes.
gaps.suggested_search_query: "email prioritization" "response obligation" hard constraints soft preferences personalized triage reminder
gaps.resolution_notes: Still open. The admitted literature separately supports importance, urgency, social/contextual priority, reminder value, and prospective-memory signals, but does not experimentally compare policies that keep explicit obligations or user rules distinct from learned preference signals.

gaps.description: Long-term adaptation to changing user roles, projects, priorities, feedback, and work patterns is not directly evaluated in the admitted personalized workplace email or reminder studies.
gaps.suggested_search_query: "longitudinal personalization" workplace email preference drift adaptive prioritization user feedback
gaps.resolution_notes: Still open. Temporal recommender and interactive preference-learning work supplies adjacent mechanisms, but sustained adaptation to changing workplace roles, projects, priorities, and communication patterns has not been directly evaluated.

gaps.description: The corpus does not provide an end-to-end evaluation of briefing content selection that jointly measures omission of decision-essential work, redundant repetition, false alerts, and preservation of unresolved important state over repeated cycles.
gaps.suggested_search_query: "longitudinal summarization" omission redundancy false alerts unresolved state evaluation
gaps.resolution_notes: Still open. Existing work provides separate metrics or objectives for temporal gain, comprehensiveness, latency, verbosity, repetition, or omission, but no admitted study jointly evaluates the complete target error set over repeated workplace briefing cycles.

gaps.description: The admitted studies do not determine how reminder usefulness or likelihood of forgetting combines with perceived importance, urgency, recency, or personalized priority when selecting content for a briefing.
gaps.suggested_search_query: "email reminder" forgetting importance urgency recency personalized priority task selection
gaps.resolution_notes: Still open. Reminder value, importance, urgency, recency-related cues, and prospective-memory effects are studied separately, but their joint weighting or interaction for briefing selection is not established.

gaps.description: No admitted paper evaluates topic- or work-item-level incremental briefing across multiple workplace conversations and sources; direct email summarization remains primarily thread- or conversation-level, while incremental evidence comes from transfer domains.
gaps.suggested_search_query: "cross-thread summarization" email multi-source incremental "work item" workplace
gaps.resolution_notes: Still open. Direct email summarization remains primarily thread- or conversation-level, while evidence for incremental multi-event processing comes from non-workplace transfer domains rather than cross-thread workplace work-item tracking.

gaps.description: Although the corpus contains evidence about stale reminders, epistemic uncertainty, and conflicting cues, it does not experimentally establish how a workplace briefing presents stale, uncertain, disputed, or incompletely investigated state, or how alternative presentations affect workplace decisions.
gaps.suggested_search_query: "uncertainty visualization" workplace decision support stale disputed incomplete information briefing
gaps.resolution_notes: Still open. Adjacent literature covers uncertainty communication, conflicting cues, and stale reminder state, but no admitted controlled workplace-briefing experiment compares presentation strategies for stale, disputed, unresolved, or incompletely investigated work-item state and measures their decision effects.

gaps.description: Candidate mechanisms from this corpus have not been compared in one reproducible cycle-based benchmark with chronological holdouts, independently labeled new/open/resolved/superseded state, user-specific priority labels, and explicit omission and repetition errors.
gaps.resolution_notes: Resolve by constructing a reproducible cycle-based benchmark from versioned workplace-message or synthetic/appropriately licensed corpora; define chronological train/validation/test holdouts; independently annotate work-item identity and new/open/resolved/superseded transitions; collect user-specific priority labels or controlled preference profiles; implement candidate selection, prioritization, reminder, and state-tracking baselines; and report omission, redundant repetition, false-alert, unresolved-state retention, calibration, latency, and cost metrics under a fixed evaluation protocol. This requires benchmark and implementation work rather than additional literature alone.

convergence.next_round_topic: cycle-based cross-thread workplace briefing with explicit work-item state transitions: evidence for longitudinal new/open/resolved/superseded tracking, adaptive personalization, obligation-versus-preference prioritization, and joint omission/repetition evaluation
